transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 min
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (CTO), Devon (Lead ML Eng), Lena (PM)

Summary: quick check-in on the SDK integration. focused on structured output stability and recent failures we saw on function-calling when payloads exceed 64k, also discussed latency numbers and next test matrix.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly checkpoint for the Atlas POC, quick roll call?
[00:14] Marta: Marta here, hi, thanks.
[00:18] Devon: Devon on the line.
[00:21] Lena: Lena here.
[00:23] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Jordan on my side too.
[00:30] Jordan: cool, agenda — review the SDK issues you logged, function-calling edge cases, structured output schema stability, and then plan for the perf runs. sound good?
[00:44] Marta: yes, please, the function calling stuff is what's blocking our acceptance tests.
[00:50] Devon: we saw two failure modes: one where the SDK returned an empty function call object and another where the JSON schema included extra fields and broke our parser.
[01:10] Priya: yeah, on the empty function call case that tends to happen when the model starts streaming and the SDK doesn't flush the buffer on a mid-token split — we have a fix in the SDK branch but havent pushed to the staging artifact.
[01:33] Jordan: quick nit, sorry, when you say "empty function call" do you mean the object is present but fields are null or the call metadata is missing?
[01:44] Devon: object present, name is null, parameters is "{}" which causes our dispatcher to reject.
[01:52] Priya: got it. that's a serialization boundary — we've seen similar with older websockets libs. our patch forces a final flush and a small delay to ensure complete token boundary.
[02:12] Lena: is that patch backwards compatible with the current SDK you'd given us? we cant rework our connector quickly.
[02:21] Priya: yes, it's a non-breaking change — it adds a retry/flush layer and a config flag SDK_FLUSH_ON_STREAM_END default true.
[02:36] Jordan: moving on to structured output, Devon you sent the sample schema for product-recs last night, thanks — we noticed two variants in the wild. can you summarize?
[02:50] Devon: sure. one schema includes prices as cents integer, the other uses decimal strings — both used in different microservices. that causes validation mismatches when the SDK returns numbers with trailing zeros or as strings.
[03:12] Marta: our parser is strict; we need a single canonical contract.
[03:18] Jordan: agreed. action: Devon will paste canonical JSON schema into the doc. note: Redwood's output sampling can be configured to strictly follow schema via the schema_enforcer flag in the SDK which maps numbers to the expected types.
[03:37] Devon: how deterministic is that? if the model hallucinated an extra field will the enforcer drop it or raise an error?
[03:47] Priya: by default it raises and pulls a structured output failure code, but we can configure it to drop unknown fields and return a validation warning instead. for POC we'd recommend fail-fast so broken outputs get caught in tests.
[04:06] Lena: ok fail-fast during POC, drop unknown in production maybe.
[04:12] Jordan: good. next, latency numbers — Priya you had the staging numbers from yesterday?
[04:18] Priya: yes, baseline hosted model (redwood-standard-1) with KV cache off avg 280ms p50, 720ms p95 for 512 token sequences. when KV cache enabled p50 moves to 220ms and p95 to 480ms. with batching at 8 the p95 moves up to ~650ms. these were on our us-west region.
[04:48] Devon: that 720ms p95 is higher than our SLA target of 500ms.
[04:53] Jordan: right — tradeoff between cost and latency. dedicated pool with pinned GPUs can get p95 to ~320ms based on similar workloads, but costs are "higher".
[05:10] Marta: can you quantify "higher" on cost? we need hard numbers for the finance team.
[05:16] Jordan: yes i'll send a cost estimate. rough ballpark, dedicated reserved capacity roughly 2.5-3x the unit cost vs hosted usage but gives predictability and lower variance.
[05:28] Priya: also quantization — if you can accept q4_0 weights the per-token compute drops and typical latency falls 10-15%, but we need to validate quality on your longer prompts.
[05:46] Devon: we have a test set for quality, i'll run it against the q4_0 model in the staging sandbox.
[05:54] Jordan: excellent.
[06:00] Priya: quick note on KV cache behavior — we noticed eviction rates spike when sequence variance is high, tuning TTLs and cache keys reduced misses by 30% in our early runs. we'll share the TTL recommendations.
[06:20] Lena: is KV cache available on private deployment too? for compliance we might need that.
[06:26] Priya: yes, KV cache is runtime-level feature available in all deployment modes, but on private/on-prem the cache persists to your managed redis or our provided option depending on setup. we'll document network and encryption requirements.
[06:45] Marta: speaking of compliance, we need SOC 2 and the audit logs detail for the private pilot.
[06:52] Jordan: i'll include the SOC 2 summary and the audit log retention options. for private we can do customer-managed KMS.
[07:02] Devon: any gotchas on data residency? our EU customers data must stay in eu-west only.
[07:08] Priya: you can pin region routing in the policy — we support region pinning and will never failover to another region if policy disallows.
[07:17] Jordan: back to function-calling failures, Priya can you explain the observed 64k payload issue?
[07:24] Priya: sure, when the combined request+response exceeded ~64 kilobytes the websocket library split frames and our SDK's parser didn't reassemble correctly in one of our older releases; that's fixed in the branch we mentioned. we've added streaming chunk reassembly tests.
[07:42] Devon: we hit that on a long catalog response. if we page results it helps but the UX was worse.
[07:48] Jordan: ok action to Priya to push a staging artifact with the fix and version bump.
[07:55] Priya: will do.
[08:00] Lena: on structured output tests — what stability percentage should we accept to move to canary?
[08:07] Jordan: recommend >= 99% schema conformance p95 across your golden tests.
[08:13] Devon: we can probably get to 98.5% today; need tweaks to prompt templates.
[08:20] Priya: two quick SDK tips: 1) set schema_enforcer=strict in tests, 2) enable output_pretty=false to reduce noise when you compare diffs in CI.
[08:34] Marta: good to know.
[08:38] Jordan: competitors briefly — you mentioned Anthropic during evals, any specific concerns?
[08:44] Marta: mainly cost and latency tradeoffs; Anthropic's managed endpoints looked cheaper for our specific benchmark but we couldn't get the same SDK features (function calling + structured schema enforcement) as easily.
[09:00] Jordan: noted. we'll include a short comparison table.
[09:04] Priya: another note: graceful degradation — if the model fails schema enforcement we can fallback to a simpler re-run with relaxed constraints or to a cached response. for critical paths we recommend a two-tier fallback plan.
[09:22] Devon: how does that interact with audit logs and replayability? if we fallback we need clear tracebacks.
[09:29] Jordan: all fallbacks are logged with the failure code and unmodified model output; the console shows a token-by-token trace for debugging.
[09:38] Lena: perfect.
[09:40] Jordan: ok recap and owners — Priya to land staging SDK with flush fix and push artifact (owner: Priya), Devon to lock schema in doc, Priya to run perf runs, Jordan to share cost/security docs — anything missing?
[09:57] Marta: could you also include an example of the SDK call pattern we should use for streaming function calls? we had mismatches in our connector.
[10:06] Priya: yes i'll include a streaming example and a non-streaming fallback snippet in the README.
[10:14] Jordan: great. schedule next deep-dive for graceful degradation next Tuesday same time?
[10:19] Marta: works for me.
[10:21] Devon: yes.
[10:22] Lena: good.
[10:24] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

Meeting end.

Post-meeting notes (auto): occasional transcription errors for acronyms and product names. Several timestamps are approximate.

Recap (plain): owners and next steps as above.
notes: SDK flush-on-stream fix to be pushed to staging
